newsitem.title: USA: Nunn interested in U.S. secretary of state post.
newsitem.headline: Nunn interested in U.S. secretary of state post.

text.p: Retiring Democratic Sen. Sam Nunn on Saturday said he would like to become secretary of state at some point in his career and would consider an offer for the job if President Bill Clinton is re-elected.
But the Georgia Democrat, retiring after 24 years in the Senate, said he was also looking forward to private life.
Asked on CNN's "Evans & Novak" programme whether he would like the country's top diplomatic post, Nunn said, "At some point in my career I certainly would consider that seriously."
"Frankly right now I'd love to be out in the private sector for a while and then consider a government position later on, but we don't get those kind of choices in terms of sequencing," Nunn said.
"If somebody offered me that position -- namely Bill Clinton who I think is going to be re-elected president -- I would certainly sit down and talk to him about it and consider it," he said.

Asked if he would consider serving as secretary of state under Republican challenger Bob Dole, Nunn said, "I'd have to sit down with Bob Dole and talk at length. I think that's so unlikely to happen I haven't thought about it."
Nunn, former chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, was one of Clinton's advisers during the 1992 campaign and Clinton followed many of Nunn's suggestions.

But the two men were deeply at odds over Clinton's pledge to allow homosexuals to serve in the military and that was one major reason why Nunn was passed over for the secretary of state job last time.
